ctx.x: Yeah there were a lot of changes in that band you told him at once I mean.

Men would come and go. No not too many in that band. My band had a lot of changes but not Troy's band. They only changed, well after yes after I left he started to change a lot of musicians to try to keep the remnants going. But when I was there it was almost a family affair because we all worked together with each other. And Scott Bagley was the only one that I could remember that dropped out and got a replacement with Herschel Evans. Because Fred Murphy didn't want to leave Dallas, Texas I tried to get Fred to…
Did he play alcohol or tennis? Alton.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: I'm referring to the great Herschel Evans... I helped him along in his music career later on when I got in Troy Floyd's band... Until Herschel came into the band.

ctx.x: Did you have a job when you left New Orleans or what were you doing?

Yes, we had a job off of us. We didn't know whether we were good enough for it or not because we only knew how to play three songs. What, do you remember what the three were? I Love You, The Sheik of Arabi were two of them. I can't remember the third one. But anyhow, after we got to Dallas, then there was a band traveling with me on the same train. It was the year that the New Orleans Pelicans were playing Wichita Falls in the Classic. And the fellas in this band, the T&T band, with some great musicians, later on…
I remember seeing a picture of Duke Ellington wearing pants like that.
